title: ConstrainedExecutionEvidence
description: Constrained-run execution evidence: cgroup limits, resource accounting, and outcome for a single budget-constrained benchmark run.

jit_representativeness.description: Whether the JVM tier under this profile is perf-representative. 'representative' = full C2; a min-footprint profile (e.g. TieredStopAtLevel=1 to fit a 128MB cgroup) is NOT comparable for cross-target throughput and is labeled accordingly.

contract_id.description: Fixed contract key from scenario.json fixed_contracts.

target_runtime.description: Deprecated legacy field. Prefer artifact_provenance.runtime_family. Retained for backward compatibility.

target_build.description: Deprecated legacy field. Prefer artifact_provenance.build_mode. Retained for backward compatibility.

artifact_provenance.description: Structured artifact identity replacing the target_runtime + target_build string pair.

benchmark_skip_target_build.description: 1 if target build was skipped (pre-built binary used); 0 otherwise.

required_track_id.description: Expected track identifier for this run profile.

result_namespace.description: Relative path namespace for result artifact directory.

soak_duration_class.description: Soak duration class. smoke=≤30s exploratory; guard=~10m; regression=~30m; contract=~2h.

cgroup_effective.description: Effective cgroup v2 resource limits and observed accounting as read from the cgroup hierarchy after process launch.

memory_max_bytes.description: Effective memory.max bytes as read from the cgroup. For native-image targets this reflects process RSS limit, not JVM heap.

memory_peak_bytes.description: Observed memory.peak bytes as read from the cgroup after run completion.

memory_events.description: Deltas of cgroup memory.events counters across the run (after - before). oom_kill > 0 is authoritative proof the kernel OOM-killer SIGKILLed a process in this scope, independent of exit code or target log strings.

oom_kill.description: Processes the OOM-killer terminated in this cgroup/subtree during the run. > 0 drives outcome=oom_killed (or oom_after_measurement when the kill landed in teardown).

oom.description: Times an allocation could not be satisfied and the OOM-killer was invoked.

oom_group_kill.description: Times the whole cgroup was killed as a group (memory.oom.group). May stay 0 on kernels without the counter.

max.description: Times usage hit memory.max and allocation was throttled/reclaimed at the limit.

cpu_throttle_ratio.description: Derived: nr_throttled / nr_periods. null when nr_periods = 0. Denominator of effective_cpu calculation: effective_vcpu = declared_vcpu * (1 - cpu_throttle_ratio).

cgroup_memory_limit_verified.description: true if the launch script confirmed that cgroup memory.max was successfully written to the correct cgroup hierarchy node before process start.

jvm_overlay_flags.description: JVM flags applied as JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS overlay. Must be empty array [] for native-image targets.

launch_command.description: Exact launch command array used to start the target process.

benchmark_exit_code.description: Exit code of the benchmark driver process.

outcome.description: Canonical outcome classification. A teardown-phase OOM after a validated measurement keeps its measurement-derived outcome (e.g. ok) and is flagged via oom_after_measurement rather than being reclassified as oom_killed.

phase_reached.description: Furthest productive phase the inner runner recorded in phase.state before exit/kill. 'unknown' when the marker file is absent (e.g. the runner died before writing it).

failed_phase.description: Phase a failure/OOM is attributed to, or null on a clean run. teardown means the kill landed after the measurement window had already validated as a real result.

oom_after_measurement.description: true when a cgroup oom_kill was observed but the measurement window had already completed and validated (phase_reached=measure_complete). The result remains valid but is flagged as teardown-tainted.

target_alive_at_teardown.description: 1 if the target process was still alive when the inner runner's cleanup began, 0 if it had already died during the run, null if unknown. Corroborates failed_phase: 0 with an OOM points at an in-run kill, 1 at a teardown kill.

memory_failure_kind.description: Diagnostic synthesis across all three sources. cgroup_oom_kill = kernel SIGKILL at memory.max (authoritative, from memory.events). jvm_native_oom = the JVM itself hit a native/heap OOM (hs_err OOM cause or heap OutOfMemoryError in the log) without a cgroup kill. jvm_crash = a non-OOM JVM fatal error (SIGSEGV/internal). none = no memory-failure signal. A cgroup kill outranks JVM-internal signals.

crash_artifacts.description: JVM-side fatal-error evidence produced by this run. Complements the kernel signal: a cgroup SIGKILL writes NO hs_err, so an hs_err here is a JVM-internal crash (SIGSEGV / native-OOM the JVM detected itself), which memory.events cannot see.

hs_err_present.description: true if at least one hs_err_pid*.log newer than run start was found.

hs_err_paths.description: Paths (relative to the result dir) of hs_err logs copied into crash-artifacts/ for preservation.

hs_err_cause.description: Fatal cause parsed from the first hs_err header (e.g. SIGSEGV, 'Out of Memory Error'). null when no hs_err.

replay_present.description: true if a JIT compile-replay dump (replay_pid*.log) was produced.

core_present.description: true if a core dump was produced in the launch CWD.

dmesg_oom.description: Best-effort kernel-ring-buffer corroboration of a cgroup OOM kill. NOT authoritative and frequently unavailable: under a --user systemd scope the buffer is usually unreadable (no CAP_SYSLOG), so available=false proves nothing — defer to memory.events.oom_kill.

available.description: true if dmesg was readable for this run.

oom_killer_invoked.description: true if OOM-killer lines matched, false if none matched, null when dmesg was unavailable.

matched_line_count.description: Number of OOM-related lines matched (capped sample).

sample_lines.description: Up to 15 matched OOM-killer lines (tail), for triage.

generated_at_utc.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp when this evidence file was generated.
